the p16INK4A gene is paradoxically down-regulated in AML blasts with advancing age, which might contribute to the higher incidence of AML in elderly patients.
the expression of p16 is paradoxically down-regulated in AML with advancing age.
p16INK4A expression is paradoxically downregulated with increasing age in AML.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that underlie the age-associated changes in gene expression in healthy individuals and cancer patients.
the study of the role of aging in cancer development and progression.
the identification of the mechanisms that underlie the down-regulation of the tumor suppressor gene p16INK4 in older AML patients.

p16INK4 mRNA levels in leukemic cells are paradoxically down-regulated with age, which is a novel observation that needs further investigation to clarify the underlying mechanism(s).
the p16INK4A gene is not a tumor suppressor in AML and that the down-regulation of the p16INKA gene with advancing age is not a result of the activity of a tumor suppressor gene.
aging and cancer share common pathways, which might be exploited for cancer prevention and therapy in the elderly population.

the p16INK4A pathway is not only involved in aging and cancer but also in the age-related incidence of AML.
aging is not a passive process, but an active process that involves a dynamic balance between the activity of tumor-suppressor pathways and oncogenes.
aging is the result of a gradual loss of stem cell self-renewal potential due to the activation of p16INKA4a and other tumor suppressor pathways.

aging and cancer share some of the same molecular mechanisms, and that aging might facilitate the development of cancer.
